topic: Niche head & neck surgical imaging AI and quantitative tasks for Margin (hnrad): perineural spread / skull base foramina, thyroid cartilage and mandible invasion, prevertebral fascia, osteoradionecrosis, thyroid and parathyroid, vascular variants before TORS, difficult airway, parotid lobe / facial nerve plane, resectability, mandibular reconstruction defect classification

findings.title: TotalSegmentator - robust segmentation of >100 anatomical structures in CT and MR
findings.summary: Apache-2.0 nnU-Net wrapper. Open subtasks directly relevant here: headneck_bones_vessels (larynx, THYROID CARTILAGE, hyoid, carotid arteries, jugular veins), craniofacial_structures (mandible, skull, teeth, sinuses), head_glands_cavities (parotid and submandibular glands, pharynx), head_muscles, headneck_muscles, teeth. Roughly 70 s on CPU with --fast; --roi_subset cuts it further. Only face/ and brain_structures need a (free non-commercial) key.
findings.relevance: This is the anatomical backbone for nearly every Margin feature in this topic: it gives thyroid cartilage, mandible, carotid, parotid and pharynx masks for free, which are the ROIs every downstream metric below needs. Adopt as the segmentation layer under the FastAPI service.
findings.license: Apache-2.0 (open subtasks); separate free non-commercial key only for face and brain_structures
findings.feasibility: Best-in-class fit: pip install TotalSegmentator, pure user-level, Windows supported, CPU supported. Requires Python >= 3.10; torch CPU wheels exist for 3.13 but nnU-Net/TotalSegmentator pins are safest on a 3.12 venv. Weights download once - needs a proxy-aware HTTPS_PROXY env var, then fully offline.

findings.title: An Imager's Guide to Perineural Tumor Spread in Head and Neck Cancers: Radiologic Footprints on 18F-FDG PET, with CT and MRI Correlates
findings.summary: Review of perineural tumor spread pathways with the classic imaging signs: obliteration of fat within skull base foramina, nerve enlargement and enhancement, and bony foraminal widening or destruction. Organized by nerve (V2, V3, VII, Vidian) and by primary tumor site.
findings.relevance: Source of the rule set for a non-ML perineural checklist: side-to-side fat attenuation and cross-sectional area asymmetry at foramen ovale, foramen rotundum, stylomastoid foramen, Vidian canal and pterygopalatine fossa, computed from atlas-placed ROIs with numpy. Highest value-per-effort item in this topic.
findings.license: Publisher copyright (criteria are facts, not code)
findings.feasibility: Zero ML. HU statistics and area symmetry inside a mirrored ROI run in milliseconds on CPU. Needs only pydicom + SimpleITK, already in the stack.

findings.title: Novel hybrid multi-atlas and deep network framework with generalizability for skull base neural foramina segmentation
findings.venue_or_repo: Journal of King Saud University Computer and Information Sciences
findings.summary: Combines multi-atlas registration with a deep network (soft attention plus a Mamba long-range module) to segment skull base neural foramina including foramen ovale and foramen rotundum on CT, motivated by CT-guided trigeminal ganglion puncture. Reports improved generalizability versus pure deep models.
findings.relevance: The multi-atlas half is the implementable part for Margin: register a labelled skull base atlas to the patient CT to get automatic foramen ROIs, then apply the symmetry metrics above. No trained network, no weights to license.
findings.license: Publisher copyright; no public code found
findings.feasibility: SimpleITK's registration framework does affine + B-spline on CPU. A skull-base-cropped registration is on the order of tens of seconds. The Mamba component is not worth pursuing on an Intel iGPU.

findings.title: Feasibility of Deep Learning-Based Segmentation of the Facial and Vestibulocochlear Nerves on High-Resolution MRI
findings.summary: U-Net style segmentation of the facial and vestibulocochlear nerves on high-resolution MRI demonstrates technical feasibility for automated cranial nerve delineation; prior work covers the trigeminal nerve, its surrounding vasculature, and temporal bone structures on CT.
findings.relevance: Underpins two Margin features at once: perineural spread along CN VII and the parotid facial-nerve plane. Important caveat - it needs thin-slice heavily T2-weighted MRI (CISS/FIESTA), not routine contrast neck CT, so it is a second-modality add-on.
findings.feasibility: Small-FOV 2D/3D U-Net is CPU-runnable in tens of seconds. No public weights, so treat as a design reference rather than a drop-in.

findings.title: CT-based radiomics and deep learning models for predicting thyroid cartilage invasion and patient prognosis in laryngeal carcinoma
findings.summary: 2D deep-learning signature on CT predicted thyroid cartilage invasion with AUC 0.835 internal and 0.804 external validation; a nomogram combining the 2D DL signature with clinical risk factors scored highest and also stratified prognosis. Notably, 2D outperformed 3D DL.
findings.relevance: Directly the T3-vs-T4a cartilage-invasion call. Use as the methodological template for a slice-level classifier over the TotalSegmentator thyroid cartilage mask. The 2D-beats-3D result is convenient for CPU deployment.
findings.license: CC BY (article); no code or weights released
findings.feasibility: 2D CNN over a handful of slices is trivially CPU-feasible via ONNX Runtime or torch CPU. Training data would have to be ours, which is the real blocker.

findings.title: CT-based radiomics features in the prediction of thyroid cartilage invasion from laryngeal and hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
findings.summary: Handcrafted-radiomics study showing features extracted from CT cartilage ROIs discriminate invaded from non-invaded thyroid cartilage and outperform subjective radiologist criteria. Open access with a feature pipeline that is reproducible in PyRadiomics.
findings.relevance: Most implementable near-term path: PyRadiomics on the TotalSegmentator thyroid cartilage mask plus a small scikit-learn model, entirely on-device. Also gives Margin a quantitative sclerosis/erosion readout even before any classifier is trained.
findings.feasibility: Excellent - PyRadiomics, SimpleITK and scikit-learn are pure pip, CPU-only, no admin. Caveat: PyRadiomics wheels lag new CPython, so plan a Python 3.12 venv fallback rather than 3.13.

findings.title: Is the Ensemble Machine Learning Model a Reliable Method for Detecting Neoplastic Infiltration of Thyroid Cartilage in Laryngeal Cancers?
findings.summary: Ensemble ML on CT reported 96.54% accuracy and AUC 0.99 for detecting cartilage infiltration, but the authors state plainly that the model cannot distinguish focal (T3) from extensive or extralaryngeal (T4a) involvement - the distinction that actually changes the operation.
findings.relevance: Cautionary evidence. Tells Margin to present cartilage output as a graded flag with the supporting measurements, never as an automatic T-stage. Good text to quote in the UI disclaimer.
findings.feasibility: Tabular/radiomic ensemble, CPU trivial.

findings.title: CT Detection of Mandibular Invasion by Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Oral Cavity
findings.summary: Thin-section 3 mm CT reconstructed with a bone algorithm detected mandibular invasion with 96% sensitivity, 87% specificity, 89% PPV and 95% NPV. Establishes both the acquisition requirements and the human benchmark any AI must beat.
findings.relevance: Defines Margin's mandible-invasion baseline and yields a concrete, zero-ML QC feature: read SliceThickness and ConvolutionKernel in the pydicom layer and warn the user when the series is not adequate for a cortical-invasion read.
findings.feasibility: No compute at all. Pure DICOM header logic - cheapest high-value item in the whole list.

findings.title: Prediction of bone invasion of oral squamous cell carcinoma using a magnetic resonance imaging-based machine learning model
findings.summary: MRI-based radiomics/ML model for mandibular and maxillary bone invasion in oral SCC, framed explicitly around the surgical decision (marginal versus segmental mandibulectomy) and prognosis.
findings.relevance: The mandible-invasion companion to the CT work. Margin is CT-first, so treat this as a second-read module for cases where CT is equivocal about marrow involvement.
findings.feasibility: Radiomics pipeline, CPU-fine. MRI ingest is already covered by pydicom/SimpleITK.

findings.title: Comparison of machine learning methods for prediction of osteoradionecrosis incidence in patients with head and neck cancer
findings.summary: Benchmarks logistic regression, random forest and SVM against a random-classifier reference for mandibular ORN using dose-volume histogram parameters. Establishes DVH metrics, not image texture, as the workhorse predictors.
findings.relevance: ORN risk module. If Margin can parse an RTDOSE + RTSTRUCT pair it can compute mandible DVH locally and apply a published logistic model, with no deep learning anywhere in the path.
findings.feasibility: Ideal. DVH from RTDOSE and RTSTRUCT is numpy plus pydicom; a sklearn logistic model runs in milliseconds. Entirely offline.

findings.title: Comparison of Machine-Learning and Deep-Learning Methods for the Prediction of Osteoradionecrosis Resulting From Head and Neck Cancer Radiation Therapy
findings.summary: Head-to-head comparison of classical ML on DVH features versus deep learning on the 3D spatial dose distribution for ORN. Motivates spatial dose on the grounds that DVHs collapse the 3D map and discard where in the mandible the dose actually landed, which matters because mandibular radiosensitivity varies by subsite.
findings.relevance: Tells Margin to store per-subregion mandible dose (ramus, body, symphysis, dentate versus edentulous) rather than one global DVH - which also happens to match how a surgeon reasons about an ORN resection.
findings.feasibility: Classical/DVH arm is CPU-trivial. The 3D deep-learning arm would be painfully slow on an Intel iGPU - deliberately skip it.

findings.title: RADMAP: Radiation-specific Automated Dosimetric dental, Mandible, and maxilla Annotation for Predicting Periodontal Problems
findings.summary: Semi-automated tool that auto-annotates mandible, maxilla and individual dental subregions and reports per-structure dose, aimed at dosimetric oral risk communication and ORN assessment. Presented as a deployable pipeline rather than a black-box score.
findings.relevance: Closest existing implementation of the per-subregion ORN feature described above. Worth fetching the full preprint to see whether a repository and license are attached before building our own.
findings.license: unknown - preprint; must verify repo license before any reuse
findings.feasibility: Segmentation step is likely nnU-Net class, so CPU inference over a mandible ROI is minutes, not seconds. Acceptable as an offline batch job rather than an interactive viewer action.

findings.title: Prevertebral space invasion in head and neck cancer: negative predictive value of imaging techniques
findings.summary: MRI predicted absence of prevertebral fascia invasion in 40 of 42 patients with a negative predictive value of 100% and specificity 95.2%; CT achieved NPV 99.2% and specificity 88.2%. Imaging is strong at ruling invasion out and weak at ruling it in.
findings.relevance: Exactly the right framing for a Margin prevertebral module: report a high-confidence 'prevertebral plane preserved' result and refuse to assert invasion. The retropharyngeal fat-plane effacement measurement is a simple HU profile across the plane between tumor and longus colli.
findings.feasibility: Zero ML. A sampled intensity profile between the TotalSegmentator pharynx/tumor ROI and the vertebral body, plus fat-plane thickness in mm. Instant on CPU.

findings.title: Neoplastic fixation to the prevertebral compartment by squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck
findings.summary: Classic source for the prevertebral criteria: obliteration of the retropharyngeal fat plane on CT/MRI raises suspicion of tumor fixation to the longus colli, but the fat plane is frequently absent in normal patients, which is why specificity is poor and only the negative read is trustworthy.
findings.relevance: Supplies the explicit anatomical rule and the false-positive caveat text for the prevertebral module UI.
findings.feasibility: No compute.

findings.title: Resectability Issues with Head and Neck Cancer (including the 270-degree carotid encasement rule)
findings.summary: Canonical review of imaging-based resectability. More than 270 degrees of circumferential tumor contact with the carotid suggests unresectability; 270 degrees or less suggests lack of true invasion. Also covers prevertebral, mediastinal and skull base criteria.
findings.relevance: The single most useful geometric metric Margin can compute: given a carotid centerline (from TotalSegmentator headneck_bones_vessels) and a tumor contour, the circumferential contact angle is elementary geometry. Report degrees of contact per slice plus the maximum.
findings.feasibility: Pure numpy on two masks - contact arc from the angular histogram of adjacent voxels. Milliseconds on CPU, fully deterministic and explainable, which is exactly what a surgeon will trust.

findings.title: Value of MR and CT Imaging for Assessment of Internal Carotid Artery Encasement in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
findings.summary: Validation of the encasement threshold: MR predicted unresectable disease with 100% sensitivity (12/12), 88% specificity (36/41) and 91% accuracy (48/53). Among patients with more than 270 degrees of encasement, true carotid invasion was found in about 71%.
findings.relevance: Gives Margin the calibration numbers to attach to the contact-angle readout, so the tool can state the positive predictive value rather than just the geometry.
findings.feasibility: No compute; it is a lookup table alongside the angle metric.

findings.title: The Retropharyngeal Internal Carotid Artery: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis of the Current Literature, and Evidence Sampling
findings.summary: Systematic review and meta-analysis pooling prevalence of the retropharyngeal internal carotid artery, a variant that abuts the pharyngeal wall and shrinks the safety margin for nasotracheal intubation and transoral surgery. Notes that few cohort studies existed and no pooled estimate was previously established.
findings.relevance: Supplies the prior probability and the measurement convention for a pre-TORS / pre-tonsillectomy carotid-proximity check: shortest distance from carotid lumen to the pharyngeal mucosal surface at the level of the tonsillar fossa, reported per side in mm.
findings.feasibility: Distance transform between two TotalSegmentator masks (carotid artery, pharynx). Seconds on CPU. One of the easiest genuinely novel features Margin could ship.

findings.title: Retropharyngeal Internal Carotid Artery Management in TORS Using Microvascular Reconstruction
findings.summary: Twenty patients with oropharyngeal malignancy and a retropharyngeal carotid underwent TORS with neck dissection and microvascular reconstruction; no serious vascular complications and an acceptable negative-margin rate, challenging the historical absolute contraindication.
findings.relevance: Sets the clinical tone for the Margin output: a medialized carotid is a planning flag that changes the reconstruction strategy, not an automatic disqualification. Important so the tool does not over-warn.
findings.feasibility: No compute.

findings.title: Revisiting vascular contraindications for transoral robotic surgery for oropharyngeal cancer
findings.summary: Re-examines which vascular configurations truly contraindicate TORS, distinguishing carotid course from the lingual and facial artery branches that are actually encountered during the resection.
findings.relevance: Extends the pre-TORS vascular module beyond the carotid to the branch arteries, and provides the distance thresholds worth reporting.
findings.feasibility: No compute beyond the same distance metrics.

findings.title: Development and Multicenter, Multiprotocol Validation of Neural Network for Aberrant Right Subclavian Artery Detection
findings.summary: 2D EfficientNet patch classifier trained on 556 ARSA and 312 control CTs, validated across two external centers and temporally: AUC 0.97-0.99, sensitivity 100%, specificity 94-98.5%. Described as the first deep-learning attempt at ARSA detection. Works across neck CT, chest CT and CTA.
findings.relevance: Best-validated single model in this entire topic and the highest-yield safety feature: ARSA predicts a non-recurrent laryngeal nerve in about 87% of cases, and NRLN injury rates are roughly 12.9% versus 1.2%. A pre-thyroidectomy ARSA flag is a genuine patient-safety win.
findings.license: Article CC BY-NC; no code or weights released
findings.feasibility: 2D EfficientNet on axial patches is fast on CPU. Since weights are not public, the pragmatic v1 is a rule-based detector - ARSA is a large, high-contrast structure whose retro-esophageal course is detectable by simple geometry on the aortic arch and trachea/esophagus masks.

findings.title: Improving difficult direct laryngoscopy prediction using deep learning and minimal image analysis: a single-center prospective study
findings.summary: Prospective single-center study using an EfficientNet-B5 model with multitask learning over picture-view information to predict difficult direct laryngoscopy. Companion work computes morphological distances, areas, angles and ratios and feeds them to LR/SVM/RF/XGBoost pipelines with scaling, imputation and resampling.
findings.relevance: The morphometric arm is what Margin should copy, not the photo arm: thyromental distance, mandibular length and angle (retrognathia), and airway cross-sectional area are all measurable directly on CT from the craniofacial_structures mask. Produces an auditable table, not a black box.
findings.license: CC BY 4.0 (article); no released code found
findings.feasibility: Landmark distances and angles on a CT mandible mask are pure geometry - instant on CPU. The XGBoost/sklearn tail is pip-installable and negligible in cost.

findings.title: Deep-Learning-Based Automatic Segmentation of Parotid Gland on Computed Tomography Images
findings.summary: U-Net variants (2D, 2.5D, 3D and multimodality) for automatic parotid segmentation on axial CT, reporting AUC around 0.96 with strong F1, precision and sensitivity. Establishes whole-gland segmentation as solved; deep-versus-superficial lobe division is not addressed.
findings.relevance: Whole-gland parotid masks are already free from TotalSegmentator head_glands_cavities. The open problem for Margin is the lobe split, and no published model does it. Our plan: derive the facial nerve plane surrogate geometrically from the retromandibular vein and the stylomastoid foramen, then classify tumor centroid as deep or superficial relative to that plane.
findings.feasibility: Segmentation covered by TotalSegmentator on CPU. The lobe-plane geometry is our own numpy code - a genuine gap and a differentiating feature.

findings.title: HaN-Seg: The head and neck organ-at-risk CT and MR segmentation dataset
findings.venue_or_repo: Zenodo / Medical Physics 50:1917 / MICCAI 2023 Grand Challenge
findings.summary: 42 patients with paired CT and T1-weighted MR plus curated expert segmentations of 30 organs at risk on CT, in NRRD format. Baseline auto-segmentation results provided by training public nnU-Net. Companion SegRap2023 challenge covers 45 OARs across 200 nasopharyngeal CTs.
findings.relevance: The validation set for any Margin segmentation claim, and the only realistic way to sanity-check TotalSegmentator's head and neck masks locally before trusting them on patient data.
findings.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 - non-commercial and no-derivatives, so usable for internal validation but NOT for shipping derived models
findings.feasibility: Download only; NRRD loads directly in SimpleITK. Watch the corporate proxy for the multi-GB Zenodo download. Note the NC-ND terms constrain any future distribution.

findings.title: A Mandibular Defect Dataset for Autonomous Reconstruction Planning in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
findings.summary: 147 clinically derived 3D mandibular defect models, each manually annotated by experienced surgeons following clinical standards, released to support deep-learning frameworks that autonomously generate reconstructed mandible models and printable implant structures from patient CT.
findings.relevance: The substrate for automating defect classification (Brown class) and reconstruction planning. Relevant caveat from the VSP literature: mirroring works for unilateral defects, but Brown class C and D defects have no contralateral reference and need statistical shape modelling instead.
findings.license: Open dataset via Scientific Data (confirm the exact CC terms on the record before reuse)
findings.feasibility: Mesh/3D model data rather than DICOM - needs trimesh or vtk alongside SimpleITK. Statistical shape modelling is PCA on aligned meshes, which is comfortably CPU-bound. Brown-class assignment from a defect mask is largely rule-based on anatomical landmarks.

findings.title: Explainable Automated TI-RADS Evaluation of Thyroid Nodules
findings.summary: Decomposes ACR TI-RADS into its constituent descriptors (composition, echogenicity, shape, margin, echogenic foci), predicts each separately, then sums to a TI-RADS level - explainable by construction rather than an end-to-end malignancy score.
findings.relevance: The correct architecture for every Margin module, not just thyroid: output auditable descriptor-level findings that a surgeon can check against the images, never a single opaque risk number. Adopt as a design principle for the cartilage, mandible and prevertebral features.
findings.feasibility: Several small CNN heads; CPU inference is fine. No released weights. Note ultrasound sits outside Margin's CT/MR DICOM core and would need a separate ingest path.

findings.title: TN5000: An Ultrasound Image Dataset for Thyroid Nodule Detection and Classification
findings.summary: Open-access dataset of 5,000 B-mode thyroid nodule ultrasound images with complete expert annotations and biopsy confirmation - substantially larger and better labelled than the older DDTI collection from Universidad Nacional de Colombia.
findings.relevance: Training and validation substrate if Margin ever adds TI-RADS assistance. Lower priority than the CT work because ultrasound is a different ingest path and TI-RADS is already well served by commercial tools.
findings.license: Open dataset (Scientific Data; confirm CC BY on the record)
findings.feasibility: Dataset only. Download size plus corporate proxy are the practical constraints.

findings.title: Slice Level Classification of Parathyroid Adenoma Using Arterial Phase CT Images with Hybrid Light Attention Mechanism Based Residual Framework
findings.summary: Lightweight hierarchical attention inside a residual network for automated slice-level parathyroid adenoma classification on arterial-phase CT, explicitly designed to stay small rather than use a heavy 3D network.
findings.relevance: Parathyroid localization on 4D-CT. Slice-level classification maps cleanly onto the Cornerstone3D viewer: highlight candidate slices in the scrollbar so the surgeon jumps straight to them.
findings.feasibility: Deliberately lightweight residual variant - a good CPU candidate if weights were available, which is not confirmed.

findings.title: Early Experience Utilizing 4D-CT Radiomic Features for Differentiation of Parathyroid Adenomas From Lymph Nodes and Thyroid Nodules
findings.summary: Parathyroid adenomas and lymph nodes carry statistically distinct radiomic texture signatures on arterial-phase 4D-CT, with the largest separation in first-order features - i.e. simple intensity statistics rather than exotic texture matrices.
findings.relevance: Cheapest possible parathyroid feature for Margin: first-order HU statistics across the 4D-CT phases inside a user-placed ROI, plus the classic arterial-enhancement and washout curve plotted per candidate. No neural network, no model file.
findings.feasibility: Perfect fit. Multiphase HU statistics via pydicom, SimpleITK and numpy; instant on CPU. Main engineering work is reliable phase identification and inter-phase registration, both of which SimpleITK handles.

findings.title: AI-PREDICT-BM: Artificial Intelligence to predict resectability and evaluate decisions for induction chemotherapy in treatment of buccal mucosa cancer
findings.summary: CNN-based model distinguishing borderline-resectable from upfront-resectable buccal mucosa cancer, reported overall F1 around 0.8. A pilot, single-site, small sample.
findings.relevance: The only direct AI-resectability precedent found for oral cavity cancer. Evidence is thin, so it belongs in Margin as a citation for why deterministic geometric criteria (carotid arc, prevertebral plane, pterygoid involvement) beat an opaque resectability score today.
findings.feasibility: CNN, CPU-feasible; no weights released and the sample is too small to trust clinically.

gaps: No public pretrained weights exist for ANY of the H&N-specific decision tasks here (cartilage invasion, mandible invasion, prevertebral, ARSA, parathyroid). Every deep-learning finding is a method description only. Margin's realistic v1 must therefore be deterministic geometry and radiomics on top of TotalSegmentator masks, with ML deferred until local labelled data exists.

Deep versus superficial parotid lobe division is not addressed by any published model - all parotid work segments the whole gland. The facial nerve plane must be approximated geometrically (retromandibular vein, stylomastoid foramen, posterior facial vein), and no paper validates that approximation on CT.

The clinically decisive thyroid cartilage T3 vs T4a split is explicitly unsolved: the best-performing models detect invasion versus no invasion but cannot grade extent. Margin must not emit a T-stage.

No dedicated skull base foramina atlas with a permissive license was located. The foramen ROI atlas for perineural spread would have to be built in-house from a few annotated CTs, or derived by registration from an existing craniofacial atlas.

Prevertebral fascia invasion has good negative predictive value but poor positive predictive value and can ultimately only be settled intraoperatively - so this module can only ever safely produce a rule-out, never a rule-in.

ORN work assumes access to RTDOSE/RTSTRUCT DICOM-RT objects. If Margin only ingests diagnostic CT, the ORN module collapses to anatomy-only risk factors (dentition, cortical thinning) with much weaker evidence. Worth confirming whether RT plans are retrievable locally.

HaN-Seg is CC BY-NC-ND, which permits internal validation but blocks distributing anything derived from it. Any future Margin model trained on public H&N data needs a license audit before it leaves the device.

PyRadiomics and nnU-Net wheel availability on Python 3.13 is the main user-level install risk on this workstation; a parallel Python 3.12 virtual environment is the likely mitigation. Also needs proxy-aware one-time weight downloads (HTTPS_PROXY), after which everything runs offline.

Difficult-airway prediction from CT is essentially unstudied as a standalone problem - the ML literature is dominated by facial photographs and ultrasound. CT morphometrics (thyromental distance, mandibular angle, airway cross-section) would be novel but have no published validation to anchor thresholds.

Automated Brown-class assignment for mandibular defects was not found as published code; the available dataset supports reconstruction generation rather than defect classification, and class C/D defects lack the contralateral reference that mirroring-based methods require.
